content.metaTitle: Sclerotherapy — Non-Invasive Spider Vein Removal | YourHealthFirst Clinic
content.metaDesc: Sclerotherapy and microsclerotherapy for spider veins and small varicose veins at YourHealthFirst Clinic, London. Dr Sofia is a member of the British Association of Sclerotherapists.
content.whatIsP1: Sclerotherapy is one of the most effective treatments for spider veins on the legs — a technique used for the removal of surface and spider veins. It involves injections with a very fine needle of a sclerosing drug which irritates the lining of the veins, causing the walls to stick together. Blood stops flowing through the veins, which are then absorbed by the body over a period of a few weeks, with the blood directed back to the deeper veins.
content.whatIsP2: Bruising can last anything from two weeks to three months depending on the size of the blood vessels treated. The treated areas can look worse before they improve as a result of the bruising — with patience, a good result is achieved.
content.fact1: High-compression stockings are worn for up to three days to reduce bruising
content.fact2: Leave a two-week period between treatments on the same area
content.fact3: Normal exercise can be resumed after 24 hours, including swimming
content.fact4: Air travel is fine straight away, though waiting at least 48 hours is recommended
content.journeysNote: On journeys over four hours it's advisable to drink plenty of water and wear class 2 medical compression stockings.
content.whatToExpectP: Sclerotherapy is not painful, but depending on the solution used, occasionally there may be a feeling of discomfort in some areas of the leg (this varies from person to person). Photographs may also be taken by the practitioner, used as a "before and after" comparison to show you how successful your treatment has been.
content.techniquesP: There are a few minimally invasive strategies for treating varicose veins, and sclerotherapy is among the most established. The procedure obliterates and destroys varicose veins by injecting them with a solution called a sclerosant. The sclerosant scars the vein and makes it collapse, rerouting blood to more advantageous veins nearby — your body gradually destroys and absorbs the treated vein until it vanishes.
content.techniqueLiquidDesc: the solution used is sodium tetradecyl sulfate, and this technique typically treats small varicose veins found near the surface of the skin, known as "bug veins", while also improving the overall appearance of the leg.
content.techniqueFoamDesc: for bigger veins, the sclerosant is transformed into a foam before being injected, since foam covers a larger surface area than fluid.
content.benefitsSubtitle: Sclerotherapy is a safe, effective and minimally invasive treatment for spider veins, helping you achieve clearer, healthier-looking skin.
content.benefit1Desc: Targets and fades spider veins effectively
content.benefit2Desc: Usually completed in a short session
content.benefit3Desc: Most normal activities resume within 24 hours
content.benefit4Desc: Helps your skin look smoother and clearer
content.howWorksP: The solution (sclerosant) is injected into the vein, causing the vein walls to collapse and the blood to be redirected to nearby healthy veins. Over time, the treated veins fade and are reabsorbed by the body, improving the appearance of the skin on the legs.
content.processHeading: What Happens During a Microsclerotherapy Treatment?
content.processP1: The first time you visit a clinic, a detailed discussion with the practitioner should clearly highlight your expectations of the cosmetic effects of this treatment. The practitioner may then take a medical history to make sure that there are no reasons why you are not suited to be treated with Microsclerotherapy. You will normally then be asked to sign a consent form, confirming that you have understood the procedure and the potential side effects.
content.processP2: The injections are performed while you are lying down. A solution is injected with a very tiny needle, superficially into the veins. This causes the lining of the vein to become sticky and swell. Compression is then applied to close the veins. Over a period of time, the vein will heal closed, be absorbed into the body, and fade away.
content.timelineImmediatelyP: Once you remove the stockings there may be marks from the needle, or bruising, and the veins may change from their normal red/blue colour to black/brown — this is all normal and may take a few weeks to settle, depending on how quickly you normally heal. 'Arnica' helps to improve bruising.
content.timelineFirstDaysP: The legs may feel slightly tender for the first few days following treatment. An anti-inflammatory drug such as ibuprofen is often helpful, and walking may help.
content.timelineAfter4WeeksP: The veins may show some signs of improvement, though results can be seen straight away — for large veins, this takes around two months after your first treatment.
content.timeline2to6MonthsP: The true effect of treatment is seen between two and three months. Some larger, darker flares may continue to fade for up to six months after the procedure.
content.rec2: The appearance of your leg is causing you distress
content.rec7: The fatty tissue under your skin hardens due to blood pressure from the vein (lipodermatosclerosis)
content.after1: Take a 10-minute walk immediately after treatment
content.after2: Wear your graduated medical compression stockings for up to 3 weeks (as advised)
content.after3: Stockings may be taken off at night or for showers/baths
content.after4: Do not be alarmed if treated veins look worse initially — this is normal and improves over time
content.after5: Avoid sun exposure on the treated area for the first few weeks, as suntanning can extend how long the dark colour takes to fade
content.after6: Air travel is generally acceptable during treatment, though you should wear your compression stockings during long-haul flights — discuss this with your practitioner beforehand
content.after7: Attend for further treatment and review of progress at intervals suggested by your practitioner
content.after8: Long-term wear of compression stockings hasn't been shown to minimise thread vein recurrence — there's no reliable way to prevent further veins forming, and occasional further treatment is likely to be required
content.tipsSubtitle: Following these simple steps can help improve circulation, support healing and reduce the risk of new or recurring veins.
content.tip1Desc: Helps reduce pressure on your veins and supports better circulation.
content.tip2Desc: Move around regularly to keep blood flowing in your legs.
content.tip3Desc: Use as advised by your practitioner to support healing and prevent new veins.
content.tip4Desc: Smoking can damage blood vessels and increase the risk of vein problems.
